author: Aaron
text:
Hi Andy,

I am so happy my analysis is helping you, I really am, however I will feel terrible if it is not the 'correct' advice. Usually if I say or mark up something wrong a senior normally jumps in to correct, so this is good.

What I marked on your chart I believe is a FL, well to me it is, some may see it as an FTR and in a sense it is, as price failed to return to the true demand below. I have marked an SR on you chart, notice how price broke through (engulfed) then based and took off, engulfing the high (you marked in blue).

With regards to your first question, I do hope I understand too

When

something engulfs something such as your high in blue I always look for the DP that broke the low or high in this case, do you see how price nearly came back to the DP? I believe you maybe right my friend with regards to the correction, price broke supply, your blue marked area and this now becomes demand, and price was just reacting from the left over orders that were there. Please don't get confused with why I placed my FL there, all I was really trying to do was to highlight a DP for you

With regards to your second question, I believe that the FTR PAZ edges are identified purely from the FTRs themselves, so for instance price engulfed into a PAZ, RT to a DP then shot of to the next FTR. I have added a chart to show what I mean, notice how price engulfed into the zone, please do not pay attention as to whether price RT to a DP or not, just focus on the fact price engulfed into the zone, and then hit the next FTR, this would be the next FTR.

Andy, I really do hope this helps, please do keep asking the questions as it helps me also. On a side note to the seniors, if I am saying anything that would be considered incorrect, please do tell me.

Cheers

DT

I am so happy my analysis is helping you, I really am, however I will feel terrible if it is not the 'correct' advice. Usually if I say or mark up something wrong a senior normally jumps in to correct, so this is good.

Thanks for your help, DT1. Reading your post I found that my 2nd question was based on false assumptions. When you said you wouldn't have traded the upper RT, I assumed that there was something special about the upper FTR level that I did not realise yet. But it became clear to me that it was not the FTR level itself, that made you reject the RT trade, but the simple fact that price had pierced it already and hence 'filled' the zone. This reveals yet another piece of the puzzle to me. Thanks a lot!

author: harshrthakkar
text: I feel the source of engulf accompanied by FTR is a stronger structure than just trading a source of engulf.Your say.

author: Hotochin
text:
harshrthakkar wrote: I feel the source of engulf accompanied by FTR is a stronger structure than just trading a source of engulf.Your say.

Yes, I do think the source of demand and the FTR is stronger than just demand alone. I have heard IF say the same thing too. The question is which level to take the trade at. If price does have enough gusto to make it through the FTR then I would say the source of that demand would be strong. In other words too many sellers would be used up getting through the FTR that they would be to exhausted to push through the source of the demand as well.

When I was looking at finding FTRs, I was always thinking of what the actual pattern meant in simple terms... A failure to return to either supply or demand, now this could be an SR, or an SD...
